In an interview with Fondo de Cultura Económica (TV show), RTVE2, April 17, 1977, Juan Rulfo discussed his novel "Pedro Páramo," stating that he "could recite the whole book, forwards and backwards." Jorge Luis Borges considered Pedro Páramo to be one of the greatest texts written in any language.

The story begins with the first-person account of Juan Preciado, who promises his dying mother that he will travel to the town of Comala to find his father, Pedro Páramo. However, when he arrives, he finds that the town is inhabited by the ghosts of those who have died before him.

The machine was a Linotype machine, manufactured by the Mergenthaler Linotype Company. It was used to set type for printing. The machine was powered by an Emerson electric motor mounted on the rear and switched on by turning a Yale key on the side. The motor ran on 104 Volt 60 Hz AC electric current, which was not yet widely standard at the time. (See "Linotype: The Film" for more information.)
